result.title: Where the Tokens Go: Heat, Entropy and Error in Agentic Coding
result.comment: 43 pages, 10 figures, 11 tables; includes supplementary information with 3 further figures
result.summary: Coding agents are billed by the token, yet software engineering says nothing about what a token actually buys. Here we introduce a theory of software thermodynamics. The theory draws analogues from classical and stochastic thermodynamics, extends them, and applies them to modern agentic coding. We count the tokens an agent generates as its cost and divide that cost into work and heat. The test suite acts as a software Maxwell's daemon that judges every coding change. We test the theory with an analogue of the experiments in which a single molecule is pulled open and let fold again: an agent makes a change to a repository (coding) and then undoes it (uncoding), many times over, and we count the tokens of every model call. The cycle returns the requested edits to where they began, with each direction started from a stored reference tree, and the spread of its cost over repeated cycles defines a software temperature, which rose with the sampling temperature of the model. About 80 per cent of the tokens of a successful run are generated in model calls that leave the requested change where it was, and we call these tokens heat. The free energy of a change, which we estimate by analogy with the equality of Jarzynski, is 14 to 22 per cent of the mean cost of a successful coding run. Coding costs 1.1 to 1.5 times as much as uncoding. The daemon is imperfect: the verdict of a test suite varies with its environment, and a suite that accepts a broken change has a cost in tokens. The practical implication of the proposed theory could be new tools for analysing and optimising coding agents through the lens of thermodynamics.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出「软件热力学」框架，把 coding agent 的 token 花费分为功与热：它让智能体反复执行代码变更与撤销，用测试套件作「麦克斯韦妖」判定每次变更，统计各次模型调用 token，并借 Jarzynski 等式类比估计变更的自由能、用成本波动定义软件温度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把「不改变状态的 token」界定为热，并量化成功运行中的无效开销与自由能占比，可能为 LVR 中推理步骤或 latent 迭代的实际贡献、THINK/LOOK/STOP 的收益成本核算和停止决策提供可核查的度量视角；论文本身不涉及视觉或多模态推理。
